findings.issue_text: Authorization check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` instead of `||` when checking isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner, requiring users to be both admin and owner and effectively breaking the feature for team bookings
No server-side uniqueness validation in addGuests schema, so duplicate emails in the input array create duplicate attendee rows

Dedup/blacklist comparison is case-sensitive (guest compared unlowercased against lowercased entries), so emails differing only in case bypass the 'already attending' filter and blacklist spam protection
Handler never validates booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/pending/rejected bookings and sending ICS files with status CONFIRMED that can resurrect cancelled events on calendars

Non-atomic write: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before updateCalendarAttendees; if the calendar update throws, a retry fails with a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error, leaving the user unable to complete the calendar update
Unhandled findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId for unassigned round-robin bookings (userId: null coerced to 0) throws a raw Prisma RecordNotFound instead of a meaningful TRPCError
Seat-capacity bookings are bypassed: attendees are created with no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and without running seat logic, so full bookings can be overfilled
AddGuestsDialog's isInvalidEmail flag is never reset on success or when the user edits input, so reopening the dialog or fixing the input still shows a stale validation error
uniqueGuests silently filters out blacklisted and already-attending emails but still reports success, giving the organizer no feedback about guests who were not added
Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name, which is empty for newly added guests, rendering a broken subject line instead of using the organizer entity
Email sending errors are swallowed in a catch block with no logging of the error object or context, making email delivery failures impossible to diagnose
Blacklisted guest email check can be bypassed by changing email case, since incoming guest emails are compared without lowercasing against the lowercased blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts:66-70)

Guests array uniqueness is enforced only in the client component, not server-side, so direct API calls can create duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate emails (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:66-78)
Team permission check uses && instead of ||, so isTeamAdminOrOwner only passes for users who are both admin and owner, incorrectly denying team admins (addGuests.handler.ts:59-61)

Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, failing or mutating the organizer's calendar with the wrong identity when the caller is an attendee (addGuests.handler.ts:150-157)
No cap on guests array length and no rate limiting, allowing email amplification/spam abuse via attendee-initiated requests (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)
Case-sensitive comparison of guest vs existing attendee emails creates duplicate records and can select the wrong email template branch (addGuests.handler.ts:68-71)
No booking.status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and a CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST re-adds the cancelled event to attendees' calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:31-48)
Seat capacity (seatsPerTimeSlot) is not enforced when adding guests, silently overbooking seated events (addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)
Guests array schema has no length cap on the array or email strings, allowing unbounded DB inserts and email fan-out from a single authenticated request (any attendee can call the mutation)
sendAddGuestsEmails emails all attendees on every addGuests invocation, causing O(N²) email volume across sequential additions and re-notifying existing attendees for unrelated guests
sendAddGuestsEmails is awaited synchronously inside the mutation, blocking the response while rendering HTML emails and ICS files for every recipient
Attendee filtering uses O(n×m) linear scans (booking.attendees.some inside guests.filter and newGuests.includes inside attendee map) instead of Set lookups
isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) check is likely wrong; should be || — team admins are denied access despite error paths suggesting otherwise
Blacklist comparison is case-mismatched (entries lowercased, guest not), allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist and dedup check, causing duplicate attendee rows via createMany
EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates may run with wrong credentials

Authorization logic inverted: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both ADMIN and OWNER roles simultaneously, which are mutually exclusive, so team admins/owners cannot add guests to team bookings

No booking-status guard in addGuests.handler: guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, causing ICS emails with method REQUEST/status CONFIRMED to re-confirm cancelled events in calendar clients and updateCalendarAttendees to run against cancelled events

Server input schema trusts client-side validation: no dedupe or case normalization of guest emails in the schema or handler, so API callers can insert duplicate attendee rows and trigger duplicate emails; validation schema is duplicated in the client component instead of reusing ZAddGuestsInputSchema
Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist entries are lowercased: incoming guest emails are not lowercased, so 'Guest@Spam.com' bypasses a blacklist entry of 'guest@spam.com'

Mutation response shape is ad-hoc and untyped: no output schema declared for the procedure, and '{ message: "Guests added" }' is a hardcoded English literal instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with the error path

EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's: when the caller is an attendee or a non-owner team admin, the calendar-attendee update runs with wrong credentials while DB writes and emails still succeed, causing DB/email/calendar divergence
No seat-capacity enforcement for seated event types: the handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but never checks it before createMany, allowing attendee count to exceed the advertised seat limit
Organizer lookup uses findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0`, which throws an unhandled raw Prisma P2025 error (500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null

Calendar update (updateCalendarAttendees) is called after the DB write without a transaction or try/catch, so a calendar failure leaves guests committed to DB while retries are blocked because uniqueGuests length becomes 0 and throws BAD_REQUEST — no retry, compensation, or user recovery path exists

Email-send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed: error logged with console.log instead of console.error, error object discarded, caller gets success message 'Guests added' even if all emails failed, and no record of which emails failed in partial Promise.all failures
Authorization check uses && instead of || when combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, meaning only users who are both admin AND owner pass, locking out team admins with FORBIDDEN

Blacklist comparison is case-asymmetric: blacklisted emails are lowercased but incoming guest values are compared raw, allowing 'Spam@Example.com' to bypass a blacklist entry of 'spam@example.com'; attendee-dedup check has the same case-sensitivity issue causing duplicate attendees and emails

EventManager is built from the calling user's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates run with the wrong user's calendar credentials — failing or mutating the wrong calendar when non-organizers add guests

Server-side Zod schema for guests array lacks a uniqueness refine and empty-string filtering, so duplicate emails in one request bypass client-side validation and cause duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails via createMany

prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws an unhandled Prisma error surfaced as a generic 500 for bookings with null userId instead of a meaningful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST

isInvalidEmail error state in AddGuestsDialog is set true on failed validation but only reset via Cancel, so after a successful retry the 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning remains rendered alongside the success toast
Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` when verifying isTeamAdminOrOwner, locking team admins out of managing guests; variable name is misleading either way

Email uniqueness validation exists only in client-side inline schema; server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows duplicate emails within a single request, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails
Blacklist filtering and attendee dedupe are case-sensitive: guest emails are not lowercased before comparison, allowing case variants to bypass blacklist and create duplicate attendees
EventManager is built from the acting caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so calendar attendee updates fail or are skipped when a non-owner adds guests
ZAddGuestsInputSchema is redefined inline inside AddGuestsDialog on every render, duplicating and diverging from the shared server schema
Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log only, discarding the error object with no telemetry or error tracking
isInvalidEmail state in AddGuestsDialog is never reset on successful add or on value change, causing a stale validation warning to appear when the dialog is reopened
BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env parsing logic is duplicated inline in the handler instead of being extracted to a shared lib helper, risking drift
Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the UI allows them to manage guests
Partial failure: attendees are persisted to DB before calendar update, which is unguarded; if it throws, guests remain in DB and retry produces misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error
Calendar update uses the actor's credentials instead of the organizer's/booking owner's, so attendee-triggered guest additions may fail or silently not update the calendar event
No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and receive CONFIRMED ICS invites for meetings that no longer exist
Server schema omits uniqueness rule; duplicate emails within one request create duplicate attendee rows since dedupe only filters against existing attendees
Blacklisted guest emails are silently dropped while the API reports success, or triggers confusing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error when all emails are blacklisted
Email send failures are fully swallowed (console log only) and the dialog always shows success toast, so users believe emails were sent even when all failed
Any attendee can add unlimited guests (no cap on guests array), enabling phishing/mail-bombing via emails impersonating the organizer with organizer's from/replyTo
Race condition: duplicate attendee creation possible on concurrent requests since check-then-insert is not atomic (no transaction or unique constraint shown)
Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is set on failure but never cleared, so the error banner persists even after correction
Organizer email template crashes on calEvent.attendees[0].name if attendees array is empty, preventing organizer notification email

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness validation in addGuests schema, so duplicate emails in the input array create duplicate attendee rows

Dedup/blacklist comparison is case-sensitive (guest compared unlowercased against lowercased entries), so emails differing only in case bypass the 'already attending' filter and blacklist spam protection
Handler never validates booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/pending/rejected bookings and sending ICS files with status CONFIRMED that can resurrect cancelled events on calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched and updated (attendees `createMany`) without any check on a booking lifecycle/state field (no `booking.status`/`booking.cancelledAt`/etc. is inspected). After updating, it calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails`. The new email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` unconditionally. So, for any booking record that still exists but is canceled/otherwise not active, this handler would still add attendees and send a CONFIRMED ICS, which can cause recipients' calendars to treat the event as confirmed again. The specific status names (pending/rejected) are not shown in the diff, but the lack of any status/state validation plus the hardcoded CONFIRMED ICS is directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic write: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before updateCalendarAttendees; if the calendar update throws, a retry fails with a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error, leaving the user unable to complete the calendar update

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). There is no transaction and no try/catch around updateCalendarAttendees, so if the calendar update throws, the mutation fails while the DB already contains the added guests. On a retry with the same guest emails, uniqueGuests filters out emails already in booking.attendees and then throws BAD_REQUEST when uniqueGuests.length === 0 with message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", which is misleading and prevents re-attempting the calendar update for those guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId for unassigned round-robin bookings (userId: null coerced to 0) throws a raw Prisma RecordNotFound instead of a meaningful TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. Since the code explicitly coerces a possibly-null/undefined `booking.userId` to `0`, any booking lacking a `userId` will cause `findFirstOrThrow` to throw a Prisma "record not found" exception. This exception is not caught or converted into a `TRPCError`, unlike the earlier explicit `NOT_FOUND` check for the booking itself, so the client will receive a generic/internal error rather than a meaningful TRPC error. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat-capacity bookings are bypassed: attendees are created with no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and without running seat logic, so full bookings can be overfilled

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` directly appends new `attendees` to an existing booking via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity/seats constraint). Although the handler later includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` and related fields in the `CalendarEvent` payload, it never enforces them before creating attendees. Therefore, for seat-limited event types, this diff enables adding more attendees/guests than the configured capacity, effectively bypassing seat-capacity logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog's isInvalidEmail flag is never reset on success or when the user edits input, so reopening the dialog or fixing the input still shows a stale validation error

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd()`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared when the user edits the emails (`setMultiEmailValue` changes don’t touch `isInvalidEmail`), so the error message will continue to show even after the input is corrected until the user cancels/closes. Also, on mutation success the dialog closes and `multiEmailValue` is reset, but `isInvalidEmail` is not reset in `onSuccess`, so reopening the dialog via closing mechanisms other than the Cancel button (e.g., clicking outside / ESC via `onOpenChange`) can preserve the stale error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uniqueGuests silently filters out blacklisted and already-attending emails but still reports success, giving the organizer no feedback about guests who were not added

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is derived by filtering out emails that are already attendees and any blacklisted emails. If at least one email remains, the mutation proceeds and the client always shows a generic success toast (`t("guests_added")`) and the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. There is no response payload indicating which submitted emails were skipped, so a request containing a mix of addable and filtered emails will still report success with no feedback about the ones not added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name, which is empty for newly added guests, rendering a broken subject line instead of using the organizer entity

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the organizer email subject interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly-added guests are persisted with `name: ""` (`guestsFullDetails`), and the `CalendarEvent.attendees` list is built directly from `bookingAttendees.attendees` without any ordering or fallback for empty names. Therefore it is possible (and introduced by this diff) for `attendees[0].name` to be an empty string, yielding a subject like "Guests Added: … with  at …", i.e., a broken subject line. The finding’s suggested alternative (“use organizer entity”) is debatable, but the underlying issue (subject can be blank due to empty attendee name) is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending errors are swallowed in a catch block with no logging of the error object or context, making email delivery failures impossible to diagnose

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The catch block neither logs the `err` object nor any useful context (e.g., `bookingId`, organizer, guests), and it suppresses the exception, so failures provide no actionable diagnostics beyond a generic message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest email check can be bypassed by changing email case, since incoming guest emails are compared without lowercasing against the lowercased blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts:66-70)

Guests array uniqueness is enforced only in the client component, not server-side, so direct API calls can create duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate emails (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:66-78)

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) only validates that `guests` is an array of valid emails, not that they are unique. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted ones), but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself (no `Set`/seen check). Therefore a direct API call with `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` (when not already an attendee) will pass schema validation and produce `guestsFullDetails` with duplicates and attempt `createMany` with duplicate rows/emails, leading to duplicate attendee records (if allowed) or a DB error (if constrained).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team permission check uses && instead of ||, so isTeamAdminOrOwner only passes for users who are both admin and owner, incorrectly denying team admins (addGuests.handler.ts:59-61)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This condition only becomes true if the user is both a team admin and a team owner, which contradicts the variable name and typical intended permission logic of “admin OR owner”. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail this check and can be incorrectly denied unless they also qualify as organizer/attendee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, failing or mutating the organizer's calendar with the wrong identity when the caller is an attendee (addGuests.handler.ts:150-157)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `EventManager` constructed from the authenticated caller (`const { user } = ctx;`), and it loads credentials with `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. The handler explicitly allows an *attendee* to invoke this mutation (`const isAttendee = ...` and the permission check allows `isAttendee`). In that case, the code will attempt to update calendar attendees using the attendee’s connected-calendar credentials rather than the booking owner/organizer’s credentials (which are available in the loaded `booking.user.credentials` but not used). This is a concrete identity/credential mismatch introduced by the diff and can cause failures (no permission to update organizer event) or unintended updates under the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on guests array length and no rate limiting, allowing email amplification/spam abuse via attendee-initiated requests (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `addGuests` mutation where `guests` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other bound (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). In the handler, any attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) is permitted to call it, and the code will `createMany` new attendees and then call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), which can generate multiple outbound emails per guest plus organizer/team emails. This creates a clear email-amplification/spam-abuse risk due to the unbounded array size and no per-request throttling logic in this endpoint. While the repo may have global rate limiting elsewhere, none is present in the diff for this new route, so the lack of a cap is directly verifiable and the abuse vector is reasonable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive comparison of guest vs existing attendee emails creates duplicate records and can select the wrong email template branch (addGuests.handler.ts:68-71)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with strict equality checks: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Neither side is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), while emails are generally treated case-insensitively. This allows adding a “duplicate” attendee that differs only by case (e.g., `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`) and can also bypass the blacklist because blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not. Separately, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` later uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive), so a case mismatch can cause the wrong branch/template selection for attendees whose email case differs from the input list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking.status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and a CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST re-adds the cancelled event to attendees' calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:31-48)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and later updates attendees and sends calendar/email updates, but it never checks `booking.status` (or filters by status in the query). That means guests can be added to bookings regardless of whether they are cancelled/rejected. Additionally, the new email templates generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (see `packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`), which can re-invite/re-add an event to recipients' calendars even if the booking was previously cancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat capacity (seatsPerTimeSlot) is not enforced when adding guests, silently overbooking seated events (addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation computes `uniqueGuests` and then unconditionally persists them via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any capacity field). Since the handler is available for any booking and even includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` on the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), adding guests can increase `attendees` beyond the seat limit for seated events, effectively overbooking without error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests array schema has no length cap on the array or email strings, allowing unbounded DB inserts and email fan-out from a single authenticated request (any attendee can call the mutation)

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` validates `guests` only as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/`.min()` on the array or any length limit on the strings. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, it uses `createMany` to insert all `uniqueGuests` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails to the organizer/team members and iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send per-attendee emails—so a large `guests` payload can drive large DB inserts and email fan-out. The authorization check explicitly allows `isAttendee` to perform the mutation, so any attendee can trigger this behavior. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails emails all attendees on every addGuests invocation, causing O(N²) email volume across sequential additions and re-notifying existing attendees for unrelated guests
sendAddGuestsEmails is awaited synchronously inside the mutation, blocking the response while rendering HTML emails and ICS files for every recipient

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after updating attendees and the calendar (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`), the mutation does `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` before returning. `sendAddGuestsEmails` builds a list of email send promises (including organizer, team members, and all attendees) and awaits `Promise.all(...)`, and the email templates generate HTML/ICS payloads. This means the TRPC mutation response is blocked until all emails are rendered and sent, exactly as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee filtering uses O(n×m) linear scans (booking.attendees.some inside guests.filter and newGuests.includes inside attendee map) instead of Set lookups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain the described linear scans: in `addGuests.handler.ts`, `guests.filter(...)` calls `booking.attendees.some(...)` for each guest, and in `email-manager.ts`, `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` calls `newGuests.includes(...)`. However, this is an optimization suggestion rather than a clear defect: the code is correct, and there’s no evidence in the diff that these arrays can be large enough for O(n×m) to be a practical/performance problem. A reasonable reviewer would not necessarily treat this as a real issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) check is likely wrong; should be || — team admins are denied access despite error paths suggesting otherwise

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, but the variable name and intended permission check (“admin or owner”) imply `||`. As written, a user who is a team admin but not an owner (a common role split) will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be blocked unless they also happen to be the booking organizer or an attendee. This is a concrete access-control correctness bug introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-mismatched (entries lowercased, guest not), allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist and dedup check, causing duplicate attendee rows via createMany

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS are normalized to lowercase, but incoming `guests` are compared without lowercasing: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows case-variant emails (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`) to bypass the blacklist. The same case-sensitive comparison is used to dedupe against existing attendees: `guest === attendee.email`, so a case-variant of an existing attendee can be treated as “unique” and sent to `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows (or triggering a DB constraint error if one exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates may run with wrong credentials

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the calendar update is executed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the requesting session user (`ctx.user`). However, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` or `isAttendee`), and in those cases `ctx.user` can differ from `booking.userId` (the organizer). That means `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` may run with the wrong person's calendar credentials (or no relevant credentials), causing incorrect/failed attendee updates on the organizer's connected calendar(s). This mismatch is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic inverted: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both ADMIN and OWNER roles simultaneously, which are mutually exclusive, so team admins/owners cannot add guests to team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the same user to satisfy both predicates to be treated as authorized via team role. Given the subsequent guard `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, a user who is only a team admin or only a team owner would be denied. The variable name and typical authorization intent strongly indicate this should be `||` (admin OR owner), so the diff introduces an overly-restrictive/incorrect authorization check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status guard in addGuests.handler: guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, causing ICS emails with method REQUEST/status CONFIRMED to re-confirm cancelled events in calendar clients and updateCalendarAttendees to run against cancelled events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler allows adding attendees for any booking found by `id` and only checks permissions (team admin/owner, organizer, or existing attendee). There is no check of booking status (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED) before mutating the booking (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sending emails. The new email templates generate ICS payloads with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), which is inconsistent with a cancelled/rejected booking and could cause calendar clients to treat it as (re)confirmation. This is directly verifiable from the diff because no guard exists and the ICS status is hardcoded to CONFIRMED.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server input schema trusts client-side validation: no dedupe or case normalization of guest emails in the schema or handler, so API callers can insert duplicate attendee rows and trigger duplicate emails; validation schema is duplicated in the client component instead of reusing ZAddGuestsInputSchema

adjudication.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema only enforces `guests` are valid emails, but does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already on the booking and blacklisted emails, but it does NOT dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (e.g. `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` will remain duplicated). It also does no case normalization, so `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` are case-sensitive, allowing duplicates/blacklist bypass via casing differences. The handler then `createMany` inserts these emails and later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original (potentially duplicated) input, and email sending iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees`, so duplicate attendee rows can cause duplicate emails. Separately, the client defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with a uniqueness refine, duplicating validation logic instead of reusing the server schema, and the server does not enforce the same uniqueness constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist entries are lowercased: incoming guest emails are not lowercased, so 'Guest@Spam.com' bypasses a blacklist entry of 'guest@spam.com'

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate highlights that the blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are not, making the includes() check effectively case-sensitive and allowing uppercase variants to bypass the blacklist. This is the same bypass issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation response shape is ad-hoc and untyped: no output schema declared for the procedure, and '{ message: "Guests added" }' is a hardcoded English literal instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with the error path

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` tRPC procedure indeed returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` from `addGuestsHandler` and does not declare an explicit output schema. However, in tRPC this is not inherently a defect: the return type is still inferred by TypeScript, and output schemas are optional. Also, the frontend added in this diff does not use the returned `message` at all (it shows `t("guests_added")` on success), so the hardcoded English string does not cause a verifiable bug or inconsistency in behavior within this change. Claiming it’s a real problem relies on a project convention or external consumers not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's: when the caller is an attendee or a non-owner team admin, the calendar-attendee update runs with wrong credentials while DB writes and emails still succeed, causing DB/email/calendar divergence

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner). However, it builds `EventManager` using the *caller* (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not the booking organizer (`booking.userId`). Then it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the caller is an attendee (or other permitted non-organizer) they typically won't have the organizer’s calendar credentials, so the external calendar attendee update will run with the wrong account (or be a no-op/fail depending on implementation) while the DB update (`prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)`) has already been committed and emails are attempted afterward. This creates a credible DB/email/calendar divergence rooted directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No seat-capacity enforcement for seated event types: the handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but never checks it before createMany, allowing attendee count to exceed the advertised seat limit

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` with `createMany` for `uniqueGuests` without checking any capacity constraints from `booking.eventType` (e.g., `seatsPerTimeSlot`). Although `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` are later copied into the `CalendarEvent` object, they are never used to validate whether adding these guests would exceed the seat limit. Therefore, for seated event types, this mutation can increase attendee count beyond the configured capacity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer lookup uses findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0`, which throws an unhandled raw Prisma P2025 error (500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this coerces to `0`, which will not match a real user and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "record not found" error (commonly surfaced as P2025). There is no wrapping `try/catch` converting that into a `TRPCError`, so the route would bubble an internal error instead of a typed TRPC error. This behavior is directly implied by the code path introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update (updateCalendarAttendees) is called after the DB write without a transaction or try/catch, so a calendar failure leaves guests committed to DB while retries are blocked because uniqueGuests length becomes 0 and throws BAD_REQUEST — no retry, compensation, or user recovery path exists

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code first writes the new attendees to the DB via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or transactional guard. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation errors out but the DB change has already been committed. On a subsequent retry with the same emails, the handler re-fetches the booking (now containing those attendees) and computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendee emails, which will make `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and it throws `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). That creates a verifiable “partial success” state with no straightforward retry/recovery path in this flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed: error logged with console.log instead of console.error, error object discarded, caller gets success message 'Guests added' even if all emails failed, and no record of which emails failed in partial Promise.all failures

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that logs only `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards the actual `err`. After catching, the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the mutation can succeed even if email sending fails completely. Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` so any single send failure rejects the whole batch, and with the current catch behavior there is no surfaced/recorded detail about which email(s) failed (and even the error object is not logged).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses && instead of || when combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, meaning only users who are both admin AND owner pass, locking out team admins with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Despite the variable name implying an OR condition, this requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that branch. Since the later permission gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, a team admin who is not also an owner (and not the organizer/attendee) will be incorrectly rejected. This is a concrete authorization logic defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-asymmetric: blacklisted emails are lowercased but incoming guest values are compared raw, allowing 'Spam@Example.com' to bypass a blacklist entry of 'spam@example.com'; attendee-dedup check has the same case-sensitivity issue causing duplicate attendees and emails

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase (BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())), but the comparison uses the raw user-provided `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. If a user submits `Spam@Example.com`, it will not match a blacklist entry `spam@example.com` and will pass. The attendee de-duplication check is also case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some(attendee => guest === attendee.email)`, so the same mailbox with different casing can be added as a "new" attendee, causing duplicate attendee records and incorrect downstream logic (e.g., `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in sendAddGuestsEmails is also case-sensitive).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the calling user's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates run with the wrong user's calendar credentials — failing or mutating the wrong calendar when non-organizers add guests

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation allows non-organizers to add guests (it authorizes if isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, or isAttendee). However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`). Then it calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. For calls made by an attendee or team member, this will run calendar attendee updates using the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can fail to update the actual booked event or affect the wrong calendar, since the booking/event references are tied to the organizer’s integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side Zod schema for guests array lacks a uniqueness refine and empty-string filtering, so duplicate emails in one request bypass client-side validation and cause duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails via createMany
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the server-side validation doesn’t enforce uniqueness within the submitted guests array, allowing repeated emails in a single request to pass through and resulting in duplicate attendee rows via createMany. This is the same core issue as the golden comment (no deduplication of input duplicates).

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws an unhandled Prisma error surfaced as a generic 500 for bookings with null userId instead of a meaningful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, after successfully loading a booking, the code does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. This explicitly maps a falsy/null `booking.userId` to `0`, guaranteeing `findFirstOrThrow` will throw when `userId` is null/undefined. That thrown error is not converted to a TRPCError (it’s not caught), so it will surface as an internal error rather than a meaningful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST. The presence of `|| 0` indicates the author anticipates `userId` may be absent, making this a real correctness/error-handling defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail error state in AddGuestsDialog is set true on failed validation but only reset via Cancel, so after a successful retry the 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning remains rendered alongside the success toast

The only reset is in the Cancel button handler. Therefore, after a failed attempt, the warning (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) will remain rendered during subsequent valid retries (including while the mutation is pending), and it can also persist if the dialog is reopened later because the component stays mounted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` when verifying isTeamAdminOrOwner, locking team admins out of managing guests; variable name is misleading either way

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass that branch, despite the variable name and intended policy implied by the later check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ... FORBIDDEN`. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be blocked from adding guests (unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee). This is a concrete authorization logic defect introduced in the diff; it should almost certainly be `||` (or the variable renamed to reflect owner-only access).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email uniqueness validation exists only in client-side inline schema; server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows duplicate emails within a single request, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guests.filter(...)` but only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails; it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. As a result, a request like `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` will produce `guestsFullDetails` with two identical entries and `createMany` will attempt to insert duplicates, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows (or causing a DB error if a unique constraint exists, which is not shown in the diff). Client-side uniqueness refinement in `AddGuestsDialog` does not protect the server endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist filtering and attendee dedupe are case-sensitive: guest emails are not lowercased before comparison, allowing case variants to bypass blacklist and create duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows case-variant addresses (e.g. `Test@x.com`) to bypass a blacklist entry like `test@x.com`. Similarly, dedupe vs existing attendees is `guest === attendee.email` without lowercasing either side, so a case-variant of an existing attendee email can slip through and be inserted via `createMany`. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` also uses `new Set(emails)` which is case-sensitive, so it doesn’t prevent this either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the acting caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so calendar attendee updates fail or are skipped when a non-owner adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` or `isAttendee`). However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user`/`ctx.user` is the *acting caller*, not the booking owner/organizer. Since the booking’s calendar event/references belong to the organizer (and the booking fetch includes `booking.user.credentials` but they are not used), a non-owner caller may not have the necessary calendar credentials to update the organizer’s event, causing attendee updates to be skipped/fail or to target the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is redefined inline inside AddGuestsDialog on every render, duplicating and diverging from the shared server schema

However, `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` separately defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` *inside the component function* as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`, meaning (1) it is recreated on every render and (2) it duplicates/diverges from the server schema (different shape and extra uniqueness refinement). adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log only, discarding the error object with no telemetry or error tracking

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches `err` but only executes `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err`, rethrowing, or reporting it. adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail state in AddGuestsDialog is never reset on successful add or on value change, causing a stale validation warning to appear when the dialog is reopened

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env parsing logic is duplicated inline in the handler instead of being extracted to a shared lib helper, risking drift

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the UI allows them to manage guests

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be *both* a team admin and a team owner to pass the subsequent permission gate:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```

So a user who is an admin but not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied, which is very likely a correctness bug given the variable name and common access rules (admin OR owner). The UI claim isn’t fully provable from the diff, but the `&&` vs `||` logic issue itself is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial failure: attendees are persisted to DB before calendar update, which is unguarded; if it throws, guests remain in DB and retry produces misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. That calendar update is not wrapped in a try/catch and not done in a DB transaction, so if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the DB changes remain. On a retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, and if all previously-added guests are now in the DB, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` triggers `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading because the prior attempt partially succeeded (DB) but failed to update the external calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the actor's credentials instead of the organizer's/booking owner's, so attendee-triggered guest additions may fail or silently not update the calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is executed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` where `eventManager` is constructed with `credentials` fetched from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. `ctx.user` is the authenticated caller (could be an attendee, since `isAttendee` is allowed to proceed). The booking organizer’s credentials are not used, even though the query includes `booking.user.credentials` (suggesting organizer creds were intended/available). If an attendee triggers this mutation, they likely won’t have write access to the organizer’s connected calendar event, so the calendar attendee update can fail or be a no-op depending on `EventManager` behavior. This matches the proposed finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and receive CONFIRMED ICS invites for meetings that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to update attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), update external calendar attendees (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`), and send emails/ICS without checking any booking status/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected). The ICS payload in both new email templates hard-codes `status: "CONFIRMED"` in `generateIcsString(...)`, so if a cancelled/rejected booking is passed in, the code would still add guests and send confirmed invites. No guard in the diff prevents this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema omits uniqueness rule; duplicate emails within one request create duplicate attendee rows since dedupe only filters against existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates `guests` as an array of emails and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering only against existing booking attendees and blacklist (`!booking.attendees.some(...)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(...)`), but it does not remove duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Those duplicates will remain in `guestsFullDetails` and be passed to `attendees.createMany`, which can create duplicate attendee rows (unless an unseen DB unique constraint rejects them). The client dialog does add a uniqueness refine, but that does not protect the API from duplicate inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest emails are silently dropped while the API reports success, or triggers confusing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error when all emails are blacklisted

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters out blacklisted emails via `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`. Any blacklisted entries are simply omitted from the `createMany` insert, but if at least one non-blacklisted guest remains, the handler completes and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with no indication that some requested guests were dropped. If *all* provided emails are filtered out (e.g., all are blacklisted, or all already exist/blacklisted), it throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `"emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, which does not describe the blacklist case and is therefore confusing. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are fully swallowed (console log only) and the dialog always shows success toast, so users believe emails were sent even when all failed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch { console.log(...) }` block that does not rethrow or otherwise signal failure. Therefore the TRPC mutation still resolves successfully (returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`) even if all email sends fail. On the client, `AddGuestsDialog` shows a success toast in `onSuccess` (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) and never surfaces the email failure, so users get a success indication despite notification emails potentially not being sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any attendee can add unlimited guests (no cap on guests array), enabling phishing/mail-bombing via emails impersonating the organizer with organizer's from/replyTo

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any authenticated user who is an existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to add guests. The input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`/cap, and the UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding arbitrary numbers of email fields. On success, `addGuestsHandler` calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which will send emails to all attendees and uses organizer-identifying headers (e.g., in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `from` uses the organizer name and `replyTo` is the organizer email). This enables an attendee to trigger an unbounded number of organizer-branded emails to arbitrary addresses (subject to only basic email validation and an optional env blacklist), which is consistent with a mail-bombing/phishing vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition: duplicate attendee creation possible on concurrent requests since check-then-insert is not atomic (no transaction or unique constraint shown)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the code reads current attendees (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees), computes uniqueGuests by filtering against that snapshot, then performs a separate prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany. This is a classic check-then-insert sequence with no transaction/locking and no createMany skipDuplicates, so concurrent requests adding the same email(s) can both pass the pre-check and then both attempt inserts, resulting in duplicate attendee rows (if no DB uniqueness) or a unique-constraint error (if a uniqueness constraint exists). The non-atomicity is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is set on failure but never cleared, so the error banner persists even after correction

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, but it is never reset when the user edits `multiEmailValue` via `MultiEmail` (`setMultiEmailValue` is called without clearing `isInvalidEmail`). The banner therefore remains visible after the user corrects the emails, until they either hit Cancel (which resets it) or successfully add (which closes the dialog but still doesn’t explicitly reset the flag). This matches the finding’s “stale validation error persists after correction” claim.
